ideas.description: Start from the E021 tip (commit bf93586: Muon + 4@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs). Change only how the Muon update runs. Wrap the whole update in a single function: momentum/Nesterov, bf16 3-step Newton-Schulz batched over same-shape filters (conv2/conv3 of each group stacked into one bmm), scale, and the weight update. Compile it with torch.compile(mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'), and pass the LR as a 0-d GPU tensor so the schedule never recompiles. Warm it up in build on synthetic gradients for every filter shape. Keep the math, hyperparameters, schedule and data pipeline unchanged. Log per-trial train time.
ideas.expected: Time about 5.85-6.05 s, which is -0.3 to -0.45 s (-5 to -7%) vs 6.331 s. The basis is the micro-benchmark: eager Muon adds ~1.9 ms/step, launch-bound with the GPU idle; compiled Muon adds ~0.8 ms/step; the run has ~392 steps. Accuracy 0.754-0.761, changed only by numerics (perturbation noise ~0.25 pp on the mean). If it holds >=0.753, it is the new tip and the base for every later cut. If time falls by <2%, the Muon overhead is energy-bound rather than launch-bound, and bs 2000 (E022) becomes the overhead lever.

ideas.description: On the E021 tip, change only the resolution split: 5 epochs at 24 px + 3 epochs at 32 px (was 4 + 4), still 8.0 total. Keep the E006 operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, antialiased bilinear downsample), AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), eager Muon, and LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count, which does not change. The compiled shapes are already warmed up in build.
ideas.expected: Time about 5.95-6.05 s: one epoch moves from 0.848 to 0.485 s, so -0.36 s (-5.7%). Accuracy 0.753-0.757 (-0.1 to -0.5 pp vs 0.7578). H2.7 predicts a loss of <=0.3 pp, i.e. a 24 px epoch keeps most of a 32 px epoch's value, which gives an exchange rate of <=0.05 pp per 1%. A loss of >=0.5 pp means the 32 px share is binding with Muon, and cuts should come from total epochs instead.

ideas.description: Explore sub-24 px phases on the E021 tip. Change only the schedule: 2 epochs at 16 px + 2 at 24 px + 4 at 32 px (8.0 total; the first two 24 px epochs become 16 px). Make the 16 px batches with the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear to 16 px). The maps become 15/7/3/1, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) handles that. Compile and warm up the 16 px train shape in build. Before the scored run, measure the compiled 16 px and 20 px epoch costs with an untimed side script (2 epochs each) and log them next to the existing cost table.
ideas.expected: 16 px epoch cost <=0.35x a 32 px epoch (~0.25-0.30 s), giving time about 5.85-6.0 s (-5 to -8% vs 6.331). Accuracy 0.752-0.758 (-0.0 to -0.6 pp). If the loss is <=0.3 pp, the very-low-res phase is the cheapest epoch source, and the next step reinvests the savings in +1 epoch. If the 16 px cost is >0.4x (small maps underuse the GPU) or the loss is >=0.5 pp, H2.8 is refuted.

ideas.description: Rebased I026. On the E021 tip, change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.85 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24 unchanged). The 0.6/0.24 values come from CIFAR-10 airbench94 at bs 2000. At bs 1024 each step averages half as many examples, which usually favors higher momentum. Leave the SGD groups, schedule and resolution split unchanged.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.5 pp vs 0.7578. A gain of >=0.3 pp is worth ~0.5 Muon-epochs (~5% of time) at zero cost and should then stack with the compiled-Muon tip. A loss means momentum 0.6 is near-optimal, and lr is the next Muon knob to tune.

ideas.description: Rebased I025. On the E021 tip, replace every exact GELU with nn.GELU(approximate='tanh'). Change nothing else, and recompile/warm up both train shapes and eval in build.
ideas.expected: Time -0.5 to -1.5% (about 6.24-6.30 s), because the fused BN+activation kernels use less energy (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7578. If time falls by <0.5%, the erf is not an energy driver and elementwise micro-tuning is closed.

ideas.description: Margin check on the current tip, with no recipe change. Using an untimed side script, run the E021 submission through the benchmark's own trial code (import it, do not edit benchmark/) on extra seeds 3-10, and record per-seed accuracy and time. The scored run is unchanged (just repeat E021) so the loop has a row, or skip scoring if the harness allows. This gauges whether the 3-seed 0.7578 reflects the 40-seed mean before margin is spent on cuts (the tip's seed 2 was 0.7523).
ideas.expected: Mean over seeds 3-10 is 0.754-0.759, std ~0.3-0.4 pp, so the tip clears the official 75% with ~0.4+ pp to spare, and future cut rounds may spend down to ~0.755 on seeds 0-2. If the mean is <0.752, seeds 0-2 are a favorable draw, and future tips need a 3-seed mean >=0.757.

ideas.description: Observational, on the E021 tip with no recipe change. During one scored run, sample board power and SM clock via NVML at >=10 Hz in a separate monitoring process launched outside the submission (no sleeps inside submission code). Tag the samples by phase using logged CUDA-event timestamps for the 24 px phase, the 32 px phase and the eager Muon steps. Report the fraction of time at >=95% of the 400 W cap for each phase.
ideas.expected: The 32 px phase sits at the cap for >=80% of its time. The 24 px phase sits below 90% of the cap for >=30% of its time, because its small maps plus eager Muon launches leave GPU gaps. That would predict compiled Muon saves proportionally more in the 24 px phase, and that overhead fixes (H3-style) matter again under low-res training. Accuracy and time identical to E021 (±0.5%).

drop.reason: Its base is out of date: it was written for E019 (8.5-ep SGD-schedule Muon, 8.04 s). It is re-proposed on the E021 tip (Muon + 24->32 px), so any time saving lands on the recipe that is actually scored.
Its base is out of date: it targets the I022/E020 recipe, which E021 has superseded. It is re-proposed as Muon momentum 0.85 on the E021 tip.

structured_output.summary: The tip is E021 (Muon + 4@24/4@32 px, 8 epochs: 0.7578, 6.331 s), with 0.48 pp of margin. The top exploit is a compiled, shape-batched Muon step. Eager Muon adds ~1.9 ms/step, mostly launch-bound, and compiling it should save ~0.4 s at no accuracy cost. Next: shift the split to 5@24/3@32 (H2.7, -0.36 s), then explore 16 px first epochs (H2.8.1). Muon momentum 0.85 and tanh-GELU are rebased from older recipes onto the tip, and stale I025/I026 are dropped. For risk control, an extra-seed check (seeds 3-10) on the tip calibrates how much margin later cuts can spend. An NVML observation tests whether the 24 px phase is power-capped (H2.4.1).
